description_ru: Комический рассказ об офисной кухне, где пропавший йогурт перерос в настоящий конфликт отделов.
text:
It began, as all great wars do, with a yogurt. On a grey Tuesday in March, a mild-mannered accountant named Gerald opened the fridge on the third floor, reached for his strawberry yogurt and found only a spoon, which had been left in the empty pot like a flag planted on conquered ground. Gerald stood perfectly still. Then he went back to his desk and wrote an email with the subject line "Whoever you are", which, as everyone who works in an office knows, is the first shot of any serious conflict.

The email was sent to the entire floor. In it, Gerald stated that he was not an angry man, that he had worked at the company for eleven years, and that he had never before felt the need to put his name on his lunch. He added, in a paragraph that was later widely quoted, that a person who steals a yogurt is a person who is capable of anything. Within an hour, he had received fourteen replies, and none of them was an apology. Two of them were from people who wanted to know whether the yogurt had really been strawberry.

By Wednesday, the fridge had been divided into territories. The marketing department, who had always considered themselves to be creative, covered their shelf with drawings of skulls and little notices that said "Hands off". The sales team, who were louder, stuck up a laminated sign that read "This is a Safe Space for Sandwiches". The people from IT, who never said much, installed a small camera above the milk, and nobody could tell whether it was real. Somebody had labelled a lettuce in capital letters. Somebody else had labelled a single grape.

On Thursday, the situation escalated. A rumour, which was probably started by a man from accounts, spread that the thief was Brenda from reception. Brenda, who had been at the company for twenty-three years and who brought in homemade cakes every Friday, was understandably upset. She replied to the whole floor, saying that she had never touched a yogurt in her life, and that she preferred her desserts to have a bit more character. The cakes did not appear on Friday, and the mood in the building darkened considerably.

The management, of course, tried to remain neutral. A memo was sent out, which was signed by someone from Human Resources and entitled "Shared Refrigeration: A Community Responsibility". It contained eleven rules, one of which was that all food must be clearly named, dated and, in the case of anything with a strong smell, apologised to in writing. Employees were reminded that the fridge would be emptied every Friday at five o'clock. This was taken, correctly, as a declaration of war on everybody.

Friday at five o'clock was chaos. A small crowd had gathered round the fridge, each person guarding a carrier bag as if it contained the crown jewels. A man from logistics was seen smuggling out half a roast chicken in his coat. The cleaner, a calm woman named Dolores who had seen far worse in her time, opened the door, looked inside and calmly threw away a cheese that had been growing a beard since January. There was a gasp. A voice shouted, "That was an experiment!" It was never established whose.

It was Dolores, in the end, who solved the mystery. On Monday morning, as she was mopping the floor, she noticed a small empty pot in the pocket of a coat which had been hung on the back of a chair. The coat, according to witnesses, belonged to Gerald himself. It appeared that he had eaten the yogurt on the Monday, at about eleven o'clock, during a particularly dull meeting, and had completely forgotten. The spoon, which had so insulted him, had been put back by his own hand.

Dolores showed him the pot and said nothing. This, he later explained, was the worst part of all. For several minutes he stared at it. Then he began to laugh, in the quiet, hopeless way of a man who has accused an innocent receptionist of theft, and who is about to be forgiven by nobody. He walked down to reception with a large box of cakes from the bakery on the corner, and he apologised to Brenda in front of the whole floor, using words that were later described by those present as "extremely long".

Peace was restored. The skulls were taken down, the camera turned out to be a smoke alarm and the lettuce was eaten at last, by a vegetarian called Hugo, who said that it had been waiting long enough. A new sign was put on the fridge door. It was written by Gerald himself, and it said, in large friendly letters: "If you borrow my yogurt, please tell me. I might have eaten it already."

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Короткий краткий звук между «а» и «э», рот открыт слабо; не «о».
Задняя часть языка к мягкому нёбу, звук идёт через нос; не добавляйте «г» в конце.
Ударение ставьте на нужный слог: ударный слог длиннее, громче и выше по тону, остальные сокращаются.
В конце слова и перед согласной «l» твёрдое: кончик языка вверху, спинка оттянута назад.

questions.question: Who solved the mystery and how?
questions.answer: Dolores the cleaner found the empty pot in Gerald's coat pocket.

questions.question: How did Gerald make peace?
questions.answer: He apologised to Brenda with a box of cakes and put up a friendly sign.
